pool.q: A primary key is
options: a value used to identify one specific row in a table
a value used to make values unique
a value used to force capitalization

pool.q: A foreign key is used to
options: values that reference the ids in a separate table
values that reference the strings in a separate table
preserve values that change over time

pool.q: A numeric 'ID' column would be a good primary key
Which one of these is NOT a type of NoSQL?
What do you use to do calculations in spreadsheets?
What other type of non-relational data does a document in a document database resemble?
What does 'polyglot persistence' mean?
options: Storing every dataset in one relational database
Selecting multiple storage models for different needs in one system
Writing pipelines in several programming languages
Keeping several backups of the same table
pool.explain: Most production systems mix relational, document, key-value and other stores, each where it fits best.
pool.evidence: Most production systems adopt polyglot persistence , which means that you select multiple storage models.

pool.q: What does the guidance advise instead of combining storage models in complicated ways?
pool.explain: Polyglot persistence is common, but each model should earn its place.
pool.evidence: Choose the best-fit model instead of combining models in a way that complicates operations.

pool.q: What is Azure SQL Database?
options: A managed relational database using the SQL Server engine
pool.explain: It suits structured data with relationships and transactions.
pool.evidence: SQL Database is a managed relational database for modern cloud applications that use the SQL Server engine.

pool.q: In transaction processing (OLTP), what does atomicity mean?
options: Each value is stored in its own column
Transactions run on a single atomic clock
An entire transaction succeeds or fails as one unit and is never left half-completed
Only one user can write at a time
pool.explain: Atomicity is the 'A' of ACID — no partial updates are ever visible.
pool.evidence: Atomicity means that an entire transaction always succeeds or fails as one unit of work, and is never left in a half-completed state.

pool.q: What is online analytical processing (OLAP) for?
options: Organising large business databases to perform complex calculations and trend analysis
Recording individual sales as they happen
pool.explain: OLAP serves read-heavy analytics; OLTP databases are optimised for individual record entries.
pool.evidence: Online analytical processing (OLAP) is a technology that organizes large business databases to perform complex calculations and trend analysis.

pool.q: Why are transaction (OLTP) databases poorly suited to analysis?
options: They are built for individual record entries, so analytical retrieval is slow and difficult
pool.explain: OLAP systems reorganise the data for complex calculations and trends.
pool.evidence: These databases hold valuable information, but they're not designed for analysis, so data retrieval is time-consuming and difficult.

pool.q: What does a semantic data model provide?
options: A layer of abstraction so users needn't know the underlying data structures
pool.explain: Columns often get friendlier names that make their meaning obvious.
pool.evidence: Semantic modeling provides a level of abstraction over the database schema so that users don't need to know the underlying data structures.

pool.q: What is ETL?
options: A way to encrypt, transfer and log files
A data integration process that consolidates data from diverse sources into a unified data store
pool.explain: Extract from sources, transform with business rules, load into a target store.
pool.evidence: Extract, transform, load (ETL) is a data integration process that consolidates data from diverse sources into a unified data store.

pool.q: How does ELT differ from ETL?
options: The target data store's own processing transforms the data, not a separate engine
pool.explain: Data is loaded first and transformed inside the destination.
pool.evidence: Instead of using a separate transformation engine, the processing capabilities of the target data store are used to transform data.

pool.q: What is one benefit of the ELT approach?
options: It needs no storage at all
It removes the need for business rules
It works only with small data
Scaling the target data store also scales the pipeline's performance
pool.explain: Transformation power grows with the data store.
pool.evidence: Another benefit to this approach is that scaling the target data store also scales the ELT pipeline performance.

pool.q: If you need big data capabilities to move and transform data, what kind of service should you choose?
options: A script on a single laptop
A cloud-based service that doesn't depend on local processing power
pool.explain: Cloud services scale beyond what one machine can process.
pool.evidence: If you do, choose a cloud-based service that doesn't depend on your local processing power.

pool.q: How does a data lake hold data?
options: Only after it has been cleaned and modelled
In large volumes in its native, raw format
In a single spreadsheet per department
pool.explain: Data lakes keep data untransformed and apply transformation only when the data is needed.
pool.evidence: A data lake is a storage repository that holds large volumes of data in its native, raw format.

pool.q: When does a data lake apply transformations to data?
options: Only when the data is needed
pool.explain: Keeping raw data is valuable when future insights aren't known yet.
pool.evidence: Data lakes store all data types in their original, untransformed state and apply transformation only when the data is needed.

pool.q: What is the medallion architecture?
options: A layered design (bronze, silver, gold) that improves quality, governance and performance
A ranking of the best databases
pool.explain: Data is refined as it moves from one layer to the next.
pool.evidence: This layered design, known as the medallion architecture

pool.q: What does the raw (bronze) layer of a data lake store?
options: Ingested data in its original format, with minimal transformation
pool.explain: Later layers clean and aggregate it for analytics.
pool.evidence: Stores ingested data in its original format with minimal transformation.

pool.q: What is a big data architecture designed to handle?
options: Data too large or complex for traditional database systems
pool.explain: It covers ingestion, processing and analysis at scale.
pool.evidence: A big data architecture is designed to handle the ingestion, processing, and analysis of data that's too large or complex for traditional database systems.

pool.q: When is batch processing the right choice?
options: When data must be prepared for reports on past events or trends
When there is very little data
pool.explain: Real-time needs call for stream processing instead.
pool.evidence: When data needs to be prepared for analysis and made available for reports that reflect past events or trends, batch processing is useful.

pool.q: If a solution has real-time data sources, what must its architecture include?
options: A way to capture and store real-time messages for stream processing
pool.explain: Message ingestion services buffer events for stream processors.
pool.evidence: the architecture must include a way to capture and store real-time messages for stream processing

pool.q: Which of these is an option for capturing real-time messages?
pool.explain: Azure Event Hubs and IoT Hub are other options.
pool.evidence: Options include Fabric Real-Time Intelligence eventstreams, Azure Event Hubs, Azure IoT Hub, and Apache Kafka.

pool.q: What is the fundamental requirement of batch processing engines?
options: To answer each query in milliseconds
To store data in its raw format
To scale out computations to handle a large volume of data
To run only once a year
pool.explain: Batch jobs process large, bounded datasets, so they must scale out across many machines.
pool.evidence: The fundamental requirement of batch processing engines is to scale out computations to handle a large volume of data.

pool.q: How is streaming data produced?
options: At high volume in a continuous, incremental manner that can be processed in near real-time
Only when a user requests a report
As a single snapshot of a database
pool.explain: Stream processing handles unbounded data as it arrives, often with validation logic for errors.
pool.evidence: Streaming data is emitted at high volume in a continuous, incremental manner that can be processed in near real-time.

pool.q: Why do stream processing systems usually include data validation logic?
options: To catch errors in data that arrives continuously
pool.explain: Streaming data can be malformed, duplicated or out of order.
pool.evidence: So stream processing and analytics systems typically include logic for data validation to mitigate these errors.

pool.q: How can stream producers cope with network disruptions or broker failures?
pool.explain: Retries make data delivery dependable.
pool.evidence: Producers can manage network disruptions or broker failures through automatic retries to ensure dependable data delivery.

pool.q: What are facets in OpenRefine useful for?
options: Getting an overview of the data and making it more consistent
pool.explain: They summarise and filter the values in a column.
pool.evidence: Facets are one of the most useful features of OpenRefine and can help both get an overview of the data in a project as well as help you bring more consistency to the data.

pool.q: What does a scatterplot facet let you do?
options: Filter by combinations of values in two numeric columns
pool.explain: Numeric and scatterplot facets display graphs instead of lists.
pool.evidence: A scatterplot facet allows you to visualise values in a pair of numeric columns as a scatterplot, so that you can filter by two-value combinations.

pool.q: Why try more than one clustering algorithm in OpenRefine?
options: Only one algorithm works for text
Different algorithms can give different results
pool.explain: Some near-duplicates are only caught by a different method.
pool.evidence: Understand that there are different clustering algorithms which might give different results.

pool.q: Which facets display graphs instead of lists of values?
pool.explain: Graphs make it easy to spot outliers and ranges.
pool.evidence: Numeric and Scatterplot facets display graphs instead of lists of values.

pool.q: When a table is imported into OpenRefine, how are its columns treated at first?
options: All columns are treated as containing text values
pool.explain: You must transform a column to numbers explicitly before numeric facets make sense.
pool.evidence: When a table is imported into OpenRefine, all columns are treated as containing text values.

pool.q: Why can an OpenRefine cleaning process be reapplied to another dataset?
options: Because it only works on CSV files
Because OpenRefine saves every change you make, and the steps can be exported as JSON and imported elsewhere
Because it uploads data to the cloud
pool.explain: The recorded history is a script you can export and replay — a repeatable pipeline step.
pool.evidence: OpenRefine saves every change you make to the dataset.
